notes.meaning: John introduces himself simply as the elder because of his advanced age and his well-known leadership among the churches. He writes to a Christian woman and her children, whom he and all true believers love because of the truth of the gospel. Christian love is not just a polite feeling, but a deep bond shared by everyone who knows God's truth.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following early church writers like Jerome, many Catholic interpreters understand the chosen lady as a symbolic figure for a local church and her children as its members.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the recipient was a specific woman of means who hosted and led a house church in her home.

notes.meaning: John explains that Christian love rests on the truth of God's word living inside believers. This truth is more than mere facts; it is the living presence of God and His Spirit dwelling within His people. Because God's truth never fails, this shared bond will remain with believers forever.

John greets his readers with three great gifts: grace (God's unearned favor), mercy (His pity for our helpless condition), and peace (inner rest with God). He speaks with confidence that these blessings will truly be with them from both the Father and Jesus Christ. By calling Jesus the Son of the Father, John firmly upholds Christ's divine nature against false teachers who denied who He was.

John expresses great joy because he had met some of this lady's children and found them living faithfully according to God's word. Walking in the truth means putting God's commands into practice every day, not just knowing them in the mind. Nothing brings greater gladness to Christian leaders and parents than seeing the next generation follow the Lord.

John gently urges this Christian lady that all believers must continue to love one another. This was not a brand-new command he invented, but the very instruction Jesus gave His disciples from the beginning of His ministry. Faithful discipleship always comes back to this ongoing call to love our brothers and sisters in Christ.

John explains that genuine love is shown by actively obeying God's commandments. Love is not an empty feeling that ignores God's law, but a willing heart that does what He asks. Walking in love and keeping God's commands are simply two descriptions of the very same faithful life.

John gives the urgent reason for his letter: many deceptive teachers had spread out into the world. These teachers denied that Jesus Christ came as a real human being with a flesh-and-blood body. John warns that anyone who spreads such dangerous lies opposes Christ and acts as an antichrist.

Believers must watch their own hearts so that the labor invested in their spiritual growth is not wasted. John urges them to stand firm against deceivers so they will not miss out on God's full reward. Spiritual vigilance keeps Christians from drifting away from the truth they have received.

differ.view: Believers who turn away into apostasy forfeit their spiritual labor and lose their eternal reward.
True believers cannot lose their salvation; turning away shows one was never truly converted, and the reward is God's gracious blessing on persevering service.

notes.meaning: False teachers often claimed to bring advanced ideas, but going beyond the boundaries of Christ's teaching cuts a person off from God. Anyone who abandons the true doctrine about Jesus does not belong to God at all. Those who stay faithful to what Christ taught enjoy real fellowship with both the Father and the Son.

Early churches met in homes, and traveling preachers relied on local hospitality for shelter and support. John tells his readers not to welcome or lodge anyone who comes preaching false doctrine about Christ. Giving shelter or a platform to such people helps them spread their destructive errors to others.

Giving an official Christian greeting or blessing to a false teacher shows public approval of their ministry. Doing so makes a person a partner in the spiritual damage that teacher causes. Christians must be careful never to support or endorse teaching that tears down the truth of Christ.

John had much more to say, but he chose not to write everything down on papyrus paper with ink. He preferred to visit in person and speak with them face to face. Talking together in person would bring both him and the church full and complete joy.

John concludes by sending greetings from the children of the lady's Christian sister. These relatives, who were walking in the faith near John, wished to send their love across the miles. The family of God shares a bond of love that reaches beyond individual homes into the wider church.
